summary: Checked all seven filled-in doc blocks (conversion val; seqOpsIsSeq, seqViewIsSeq, stringIsSeq, stringViewIsSeq, arrayIsSeq, rangeIsSeq) against their implementations: each description and @tparam/@return matches the actual type bounds and return type in the code, first sentences stand alone, no self-referential 'This ...' openers, backticks used correctly, and @return is correctly kept since none of the descriptions open with 'Returns' and fully restate the value. Two minor style nits found, no blockers.

items.issue: The doc comment includes a literal `@deprecated("'conversion' is now a method named 'apply'", "2.13.0")` tag that duplicates the `@deprecated` annotation already present on the declaration two lines above; Scaladoc renders the deprecation notice from the annotation itself, so the tag is redundant restatement (same spirit as the house rule against restating `@deprecated` in prose).
items.suggestion: Drop the `@deprecated` tag line from the doc comment body and keep just the one-sentence description.

items.issue: "Provides an `IsSeq` instance for arrays of any type" slightly overstates generality: the method requires an implicit `ClassTag[A0]` (`A0 : ClassTag`), so it is not available for every type, only those with a ClassTag in scope.
items.suggestion: Reword to something like "Provides an `IsSeq` instance for arrays of any type with an available `ClassTag`."
